s: Who chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission?
x: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission.

s: Which item in the 8th Central Pay Commission's Terms of Reference signals concern about a return to the Old Pension Scheme?
o: The cost of the Unified Pension Scheme
The funded cost of contributory pension schemes
The unfunded cost of non-contributory pension schemes
The unfunded cost of market annuity schemes
x: The ToR include the unfunded cost of non-contributory pension schemes, signalling concern about a return to OPS.

s: From which date are the recommendations of the 8th Central Pay Commission to be effective?
x: The 8th CPC recommendations are effective from 1 January 2026; its report is due in 18 months.

s: What is the nature of the 8th Central Pay Commission?
x: The Pay Commission is set up by executive resolution and is non-statutory.

s: Who chaired the 7th Central Pay Commission?
x: Ashok Kumar Mathur chaired the 7th CPC; Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th.

s: Within how many months must the 8th Central Pay Commission submit its report?
x: The report is due within 18 months.

s: Under which department of the Finance Ministry does the 8th Central Pay Commission work?
x: The 8th CPC is a non-statutory advisory body under the Department of Expenditure.

s: On which date did the Union Cabinet approve the Terms of Reference of the 8th Central Pay Commission?
x: The Cabinet approved the ToR on 28 October 2025; the Department of Expenditure resolution followed on 3 November 2025.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: How many quadrats of 20 x 20 square metres can be taken from an area of 20 hectares if the sampling intensity is 1%?
What is the employee's contribution under the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: The UPS employee share is 10%; 14% is the government share in the NPS.

s: What type of scheme is the Unified Pension Scheme, effective from 1 April 2025 with an assured payout?
x: UPS is hybrid, whereas NPS is defined contribution.

s: Which of the following pension-scheme pairs is correctly matched?
o: UPS – 50% of last basic plus DA
NPS – 50% of last basic plus DA
x: NPS pension is a market annuity; OPS gives 50% of last basic plus DA and UPS 50% of the average basic of the last 12 months for 25 years' service.

s: Under the NPS, what share of the corpus can be withdrawn tax-free at retirement?
x: 60% is withdrawn tax-free and 40% goes to annuity.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about pension schemes?
o: The NPS for government employees began in 2005
Employees contribute under the Unified Pension Scheme
The UPS became effective from 1 April 2025
The choice of the UPS is irreversible
x: The NPS for government employees began in 2004, not 2005.

s: To which scheme did the Finance Ministry permit Central government employees a one-time, one-way switch from the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: The permitted switch was back to NPS, not to OPS.

s: The Unified Pension Scheme carries the same Income Tax Act, 1961 benefits as which scheme?
x: UPS has the same income-tax benefits as NPS, not OPS.

s: Which group of States was identified as having returned to the Old Pension Scheme?
o: Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Kerala and Rajasthan
Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh
x: The identified States are Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. The other options replace one or more of these States with States not included in the stated group.

s: What is the minimum pension under the Old Pension Scheme?
x: OPS minimum is ₹9,000; ₹10,000 is the UPS minimum.

s: On whose recommendations was the Unified Pension Scheme based?
x: UPS came from the T.V. Somanathan Committee.

s: What is the government's contribution under the Unified Pension Scheme?
x: Government share is 18.5% under UPS; 14% is under NPS.

s: What is the minimum pension under the Unified Pension Scheme for 10 or more years of service?
x: UPS assures a minimum pension of ₹10,000; ₹9,000 is the OPS minimum.

s: To which price index is the Unified Pension Scheme indexed?
x: UPS, from the T.V. Somanathan Committee, is indexed to CPI-IW.

s: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, what is the assured pension for 25 years of service?
o: 50% of last basic pay plus DA
60% of average basic pay of the last 10 months
50% of average basic pay of the last 12 months
x: UPS gives 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years' service; OPS gave 50% of last basic plus DA.

s: On which product was a high-risk cess, earmarked for cancer care, recommended?
x: A high-risk cess on tobacco was recommended, with its proceeds earmarked for cancer care.

s: The National Cancer Registry Programme covers about what share of India’s population?
x: It covers only 18% of the population; the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions (163rd report) recommended making cancer notifiable.

s: Under the present WHO norm, cited in the proposal to make cancer notifiable, which diseases are notifiable?
x: At present only communicable diseases are notifiable; the cancer proposal would extend this.

s: The proposal to declare cancer a notifiable disease was linked with which programme and SDG?
x: The linked programme is NPCDCS and the goal is SDG 3.

s: On which date did the 16th Finance Commission submit its report to President Droupadi Murmu?
x: It was submitted on 17 November 2025, within the extended tenure.

s: Under which Article does a Finance Commission report become public when tabled in Parliament?
x: Article 281 covers laying the report before Parliament; Article 280 sets up the Commission.

s: What was the subject of Law Commission Report No. 279?
o: Usage of the Law of Sedition
Age of Consent under POCSO Act
x: Report 279 (2023) concerned sedition.

s: Which Law Commission report dealt with simultaneous elections?
x: Simultaneous elections were the 170th report (1999); 279th was on sedition.

s: Which of the following pairs (Law Commission report – subject) is correctly matched?
x: 285 is criminal defamation; 279 is sedition, 283 POCSO consent age and 289 trade secrets.

s: Who chaired the 22nd Law Commission?
x: Ritu Raj Awasthi chaired the 22nd; Dinesh Maheshwari chairs the 23rd.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 23rd Law Commission:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It is chaired by Justice (retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari.
x: The Law Commission is non-statutory, set up by notification; Dinesh Maheshwari is its chair.

s: Which committee recommended declaring cancer a notifiable disease?
x: The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions did so in its 163rd report.

s: Who heads the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions that recommended making cancer notifiable?
x: Narain Dass Gupta heads the committee.

s: How many members does the JPC on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 have?
x: It is a 31-member JPC chaired by Aparajita Sarangi.

s: Which Law Commission report dealt with the age of consent under the POCSO Act, 2012?
x: The 22nd Law Commission's 283rd report (September 2023) dealt with the age of consent under POCSO.

s: Which report of the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions recommended declaring cancer a notifiable disease?
x: The 163rd report (20 August 2025) of the Committee on Petitions made this recommendation.

s: What was the subject of the 285th Report of the Law Commission (January 2024)?
o: Usage of the Law of Sedition
x: Report 285 was on Criminal Defamation; 279 was on sedition, 280 on adverse possession and 289 on trade secrets.

s: Which Law Commission report (February 2024) reviewed the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897?
x: The 286th Report reviewed the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897; 285th was on criminal defamation.

s: What was the subject of the 289th Report of the Law Commission (March 2024)?
x: Report 289 dealt with trade secrets and economic espionage; 285 was on criminal defamation.

s: According to NCRB 2023 data, illness, the second-largest cause of suicides after family problems, accounted for what share?
x: Illness accounted for 19% of suicides, second after family problems (32%).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NCRB 2023 data on atrocities against SCs and STs?
o: Cases against STs numbered 12,960, an increase of 18.8%.
Cases against SCs numbered 57,789, an increase of 0.4%.
Over 60% of PoA cases were pending, per the National Campaign on Dalit Human Rights.
The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in 1989.
x: Cases against STs rose by 28.8%, not 18.8%.

s: With whom is the concept of the 'soft state' associated?
x: Myrdal coined the 'soft state'; Dumont is linked to the purity-pollution hierarchy.

s: Which law governs abortions in India?
x: Abortions are governed by the MTP Act.

s: Which State had the highest share of illness-related suicides in 2023, as per NCRB?
x: Tamil Nadu had 21%, ahead of Maharashtra (12%) and Karnataka (10%).

s: By how much did crimes against Scheduled Tribes rise in 2023, according to NCRB?
x: ST atrocities rose 28.8%; SC atrocities only 0.4%.

s: According to NCRB 2023 data, which was the leading cause of suicides in India?
x: Family problems caused 32% of suicides, followed by illness at 19% (ADSI 2023).

s: Who is associated with the purity-pollution theory of the caste hierarchy?
x: Louis Dumont explained caste through purity and pollution; Gunnar Myrdal gave the 'soft state' idea.

s: Under SEBI’s proposed governance reforms for Market Infrastructure Institutions, which vertical must be headed by an Executive Director?
x: Critical Operations is a mandatory vertical headed by an Executive Director. Commercial Interests and Business Development was a vertical where an Executive Director was at the MII’s discretion, not a mandatory requirement.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, seed traceability requires onboarding on which portal?
x: Traceability requires onboarding on the SATHI Portal, along with mandatory QR code labelling.

s: Which Ministry prepared the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
x: The Draft Seeds Bill, 2025 was prepared by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The other ministries are related to economic and regulatory functions but were not identified as the ministry for this Bill.

s: The Draft Seeds Bill, 2025 seeks to replace which existing instruments?
o: Agricultural Produce Act, 1966 and Seeds Order, 1983
x: The Bill seeks to replace the Seeds Act, 1966 and the Seeds (Control) Order, 1983. The other combinations alter the titles or years of the instruments.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Seeds sold in the market – Three-year provisional registration
Varieties notified under the Seeds Act, 1966 – Deemed registered
x: Varieties notified under the 1966 Act are deemed registered; market seeds need VCU-based registration, existing varieties get three-year provisional registration, and VCU means Value for Cultivation and Use.

s: Under which system are multi-state seed firms deemed registered under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
x: Multi-state firms are deemed registered under the Central Accreditation System; unregistered imported varieties are allowed only for research or trials.

s: A concern about the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, including GM seed risk, is that VCU testing can be done by whom?
x: Foreign entities can conduct VCU testing, raising concerns such as GM seed risk; seed banks, FPOs and women collectives may also be treated as commercial units.

s: Up to what value may Vice-Chancellors and directors approve global tenders under the June 2025 changes to the General Financial Rules?
x: The approval ceiling for global tenders is ₹200 crore; the direct purchase limit rose from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.

s: Who is associated with the concept of mission-oriented procurement?
x: Mission-oriented procurement is associated with Mariana Mazzucato.

s: Which of the following pairs (country – procurement model) is correctly matched?
x: South Korea is linked to pre-commercial procurement; Germany to High-Tech Strategy and KOINNO, the USA to SBIR and the EU to the Joint Procurement Agreement.

s: By about how much are the draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 expected to cut test licence applications?
x: The expected cut is about 50%; processing time falls from 90 to 45 days.

s: Under SEBI’s proposed governance reforms for Market Infrastructure Institutions, what minimum number of Executive Directors must each MII have?
x: SEBI proposed at least two Executive Directors for each Market Infrastructure Institution, reporting to the Managing Director. The other numbers are not the minimum proposed under the reform.

s: Under SEBI's proposed MII reforms, who may hold non-executive posts in unlisted government companies or not-for-profits?
x: MDs may hold such posts; EDs may hold none except in MII subsidiaries.

s: Under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025, farmers may sell farm-saved seed, but in which way may they not sell it?
x: Farmers may save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed, but not under a brand name.

s: To what amount was the direct purchase limit raised from ₹1 lakh under the June 2025 GFR reforms?
x: The limit was raised to ₹2 lakh, not ₹5 lakh.

s: Under the draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, the processing time is cut from 90 days to how many days?
x: The draft cuts processing time from 90 to 45 days and replaces most test licences with intimation to the CLA.

s: What is the maximum fine for major offences such as selling spurious or unregistered seeds under the Draft Seeds Bill, 2025?
x: Minor offences carry up to ₹2 lakh; major offences up to ₹30 lakh, with cancellation or imprisonment.

s: Which body is the drug regulator under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019?
x: CDSCO is the regulator; the draft amendments replace the test licence with intimation to the Central Licensing Authority.

s: India's tiger population, cited in the Tribal Affairs Ministry's conservation policy, rose from about 1,411 in 2006 to over how many in 2023?
x: Tigers increased from about 1,411 in 2006 to over 3,000 in 2023.

s: Under the UK's Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, 2024, whose approval was required?
x: The Bill required High Court approval, not Supreme Court approval, and excluded mental illness and disability.

s: Under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ policy for tiger reserves, relocation, an exceptional last resort, cannot take place until the process under which law is complete?
x: Relocation is a last resort and cannot happen before the Forest Rights Act process is complete.

s: What framework was proposed under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ new policy on community-centred conservation in tiger reserves?
o: National Framework for Tiger Protection and Relocation
National Framework for Community-Centred Conservation and Relocation
National Framework for Tribal Welfare and Rehabilitation
National Framework for Community-Centred Forest Development
x: The proposed framework is the National Framework for Community-Centred Conservation and Relocation. The other options alter the stated title and do not refer to the proposed framework.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338A) was set up in 2004 through which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The NCST was created by the 89th Amendment; Article 275(1) separately provides grants for ST welfare.

s: In January 2025, the Supreme Court directed whom to frame a comprehensive law for domestic workers and form an expert committee within six months?
x: The direction was to the Centre, not the States; the Domestic Workers Bill, 2017 was never enacted.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about measures relating to domestic workers in India?
o: Karnataka’s Domestic Workers Bill, 2025 proposes a 5% employee contribution to the welfare fund
India has not ratified ILO Convention No. 189
Tamil Nadu’s Welfare Board under the Manual Workers Act, 1982 has a wage rate of ₹37–39 per hour
India voted for ILO Convention No. 189 in 2011
x: Karnataka’s Bill proposes a 5% employer contribution, not an employee contribution.

s: Under which Article did the Supreme Court in 2018 recognise the right to die with dignity and allow passive euthanasia?
x: The right to die with dignity was recognised under Article 21.

s: Which Article of the Constitution defines Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 366(25) defines STs; Article 342 lets the President specify them.

s: Which earlier directive did the Ministry of Tribal Affairs' policy on community-centred conservation in tiger reserves overturn?
o: The 2024 NTCA directive for mass removal of villages
x: The MoTA policy makes relocation a last resort and overturns the 2024 NTCA directive for mass removal of villages.

s: Which ILO Convention on domestic workers has India voted for but not ratified?
x: India voted for ILO Convention C189 (2011) on domestic workers but has not ratified it.

s: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution applies to tribal areas in which States?
o: Meghalaya, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur
x: Under Article 244(2), the Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides grants-in-aid from the Union for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 275(1) provides grants for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Tribal Affairs set up?
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999.

s: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are implemented through which body?
x: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs are run through TRIFED.

s: The Union Health Ministry’s recommendations on organ transplantation included mandatory data sharing with which organisation?
x: The recommendation was mandatory data sharing with NOTTO. Co-WIN and U-WIN are immunisation platforms, while DigiLocker is used for the CBSE marksheet facility.

s: Which country's model does India's front-of-pack labelling to fight non-communicable diseases follow?
x: Front-of-pack labelling follows the Singapore model, not Thailand's.

s: How many kidney transplants did India record in 2024–25, against a demand of over one lakh?
x: India recorded 13,476 kidney transplants in 2024–25 against demand of over one lakh.

s: With which chemical was Coldrif cough syrup, linked to the deaths of at least 16 children in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, contaminated?
x: The syrup contained diethylene glycol, confirmed by the Tamil Nadu Drugs Control laboratory; CDSCO recommended cancelling the licence.

s: After the Coldrif cough syrup deaths, the Health Ministry stressed compliance with which requirement?
o: Revised Schedule M on Good Manufacturing Practices
x: The Health Ministry stressed strict compliance with revised Schedule M on Good Manufacturing Practices.

s: In which country did a diethylene glycol cough-syrup incident kill over 60 children in 2022?
x: The 2022 incident was in Gambia; the 2023 incident was in Uzbekistan.

s: Which development is highlighted as part of the triple burden of malnutrition in India?
x: The triple burden of malnutrition includes the trend of obesity overtaking underweight. The alternatives reverse or exaggerate the reported development.

s: According to UNICEF India, non-communicable diseases cause what share of deaths in India?
x: NCDs cause 63% of deaths in India; 25–26% refers to premature NCD deaths.

s: The first human H5N1 death reported in Andhra Pradesh involved which of the following?
o: A two-year-old girl from Palnadu district
A two-year-old boy from Palnadu district
A two-year-old girl from Guntur district
A five-year-old girl from Palnadu district
x: The deceased was a two-year-old girl from Palnadu district, making it the first human H5N1 death in Andhra Pradesh. The other options alter the child’s sex, district or age.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the human H5N1 death in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The child died on 16 March at AIIMS-Mangalagiri.
Infection was confirmed on 31 March by NIV, Pune.
The child's contacts tested positive for H5N1.
x: The child's contacts tested negative for H5N1.

s: The first human H5N1 death reported in Andhra Pradesh was likely associated with which suspected source of infection?
x: The suspected source was the child’s habit of eating raw chicken. Palnadu had not reported an earlier bird-flu outbreak, making that the reported likely source rather than the other listed possibilities.

s: Which statement correctly describes H5N1 in the context of the reported Andhra Pradesh case?
o: It is highly pathogenic avian influenza, and human-to-human transmission remains unconfirmed
It is a low-pathogenic avian influenza, and human-to-human transmission is confirmed
It is a form of leptospirosis, and human-to-human transmission is confirmed
It is a bacterial respiratory infection, and human-to-human transmission remains unconfirmed
x: H5N1 stands for highly pathogenic avian influenza, while human-to-human transmission has not been confirmed. The other options incorrectly change either the nature of the disease or the status of transmission.

s:
Assertion (A): India is the second-largest pharmaceutical producer by volume.
Reason (R): India supplies pharmaceuticals to 200+ countries.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is false because India ranks third by pharmaceutical volume, not second. Reason R is true because India supplies pharmaceuticals to 200+ countries, but that fact does not establish the volume ranking.

s: Which lab confirmed diethylene glycol contamination in Coldrif cough syrup?
x: The Tamil Nadu Drugs Control lab confirmed it; CDSCO recommended cancelling the licence.

s: By what proportion does SDG 3.4 aim to reduce premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by 2030?
x: SDG 3.4 targets a one-third cut in premature NCD mortality by 2030.

s: Under which Act are drugs and cosmetics regulated in India?
x: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 is the main law; Schedule M sets Good Manufacturing Practices.

s: Which institute confirmed the first human H5N1 death in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The case from Palnadu, India's second human H5N1 death, was confirmed by NIV, Pune.

s: Which criticism was made of the UGC draft Learning Outcome-based Curriculum Framework embedding Bharatiya philosophy across disciplines?
o: It gives equal weight to every tradition through a multidiscipline-only pathway.
It abolishes all discipline-based courses in favour of vocational education.
It prioritises single-major pathways and marginalises non-Hindu, tribal and heterodox traditions.
It removes Indian knowledge systems from commerce and chemistry curricula.
x: The criticism was that the framework prioritises single-major pathways, contrary to NEP 2020 multidisciplinarity, and marginalises non-Hindu, tribal and heterodox traditions. The other options reverse or add claims not associated with the criticism.

s: Which clause of Article 51A refers to developing scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of enquiry and reform?
x: Article 51A(h) covers scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of enquiry and reform.

s: In which year did Swami Vivekananda deliver his Chicago address, cited in the Indian Knowledge Systems debate?
x: The address was delivered in Chicago in 1893; scholar Meera Nanda was associated with this reference.

s: Which body is developing the State Manufacturing and Infrastructure Index to benchmark States on policies, logistics and approvals?
x: NITI Aayog is developing the index to benchmark States on manufacturing and infrastructure.

s: Which institution released the roadmap for Atmanirbharta, or self-reliance, in pulses?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
x: NITI Aayog released the roadmap for self-reliance in pulses. MoSPI is connected with the AIDIS and SAS surveys, while the Government e-Marketplace and the Directorate General of Foreign Trade are associated with other matters in the current-affairs developments.

s: Which ministry conducts the AIDIS and SAS surveys?
x: AIDIS and SAS are MoSPI surveys.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed Sammakkasagar barrage?
o: It is proposed at Tupakulagudem in Mulugu district on the Godavari.
It will store 6.7 tmcft at FRL +83 m.
Submergence in Chhattisgarh was studied by the Central Water Commission.
It has in-principle approval from Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai but still needs CWC approval.
x: The submergence study was done by IIT Kharagpur, not the Central Water Commission.

s: The Sammakkasagar barrage project is intended to provide drinking water to which fluoride-affected districts?
x: The project is meant to supply drinking water to fluoride-affected Nalgonda and Warangal, besides stabilising 1.78 lakh hectares under SRSP Stage-II.

s: What combination best explains the fertiliser shortage during Kharif 2025?
o: Reservoirs being 83.5% full and stronger rabi prospects
Lower kharif acreage along with higher production and imports
Higher kharif acreage along with lower production and imports
Higher DAP sales and increased rice and maize acreage
x: The shortage was associated with a good monsoon that increased kharif acreage, while production and imports declined; Chinese supply restrictions also affected imports. The 83.5% reservoir level relates to expected rabi prospects, not the primary cause of the kharif fertiliser shortage.

s: In which year was the Free Movement Regime with Myanmar scrapped?
x: The FMR with Myanmar was scrapped in 2024, not 2025.

s: Which State gave in-principle approval for the Sammakkasagar barrage?
x: Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai gave in-principle approval; Central Water Commission approval is still required.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fertilisers in India?
o: 20:20:0:13 production reached a record 69.7 lakh tonnes in 2024–25.
20:20:0:13 is the second-largest fertiliser after urea.
Ammonium sulphate contains 20.5% nitrogen and 23% sulphur.
The Kharif 2025 shortage was linked to higher acreage with lower production and imports.
x: 20:20:0:13 is the third-largest fertiliser, after urea and DAP.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ammonium sulphate?
o: It was suggested as a substitute for urea
x: Ammonium sulphate has 20.5% nitrogen and 23% sulphur; the false option reverses the figures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the North-East's exports and connectivity?
o: The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway has stalled
The North-East accounts for only 0.13% of national exports
The DGFT 2024 export plan had a dedicated North-East section
Moreh in Manipur is identified as a gateway
x: The DGFT 2024 export plan had no North-East section.

s: Which constitutional provision was invoked in Manipur amid the Meitei–Zo crisis?
x: President's Rule under Article 356 was imposed in Manipur.

s: Which fertiliser became India's third largest after urea and DAP in 2024–25?
x: 20:20:0:13 hit an all-time high of 69.7 lakh tonnes, third after urea and DAP.

s: Which institution studied the submergence impact of the Sammakkasagar barrage in Chhattisgarh?
x: IIT Kharagpur, not the CWC, studied the submergence.

s: On which date was President's Rule imposed in Manipur after Chief Minister N. Biren Singh resigned?
x: President's Rule under Article 356 was imposed on 13 February 2025 and extended by six months from 13 August 2025.

s: Zokhawthar, a gateway for trade with Myanmar, is in which State?
x: Zokhawthar is in Mizoram; Moreh is the gateway in Manipur.

s: On which river is the proposed Sammakkasagar barrage in Mulugu district of Telangana?
x: Sammakkasagar barrage (6.7 tmcft) is on the Godavari in Mulugu district.

s: Who was the Governor of Manipur when President's Rule was imposed in February 2025?
x: President's Rule (Article 356) was imposed on 13 February 2025 after N. Biren Singh resigned; the Governor was Ajay Kumar Bhalla.

s: Moreh, a gateway town on the India-Myanmar border, is in which State?
x: Moreh is in Manipur; Zokhawthar is the Mizoram gateway.

s: What is the award period of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC award covers 2026–27 to 2030–31, not 2027–28 to 2031–32.

s: Who tabled the 16th Finance Commission report on 1 February 2026 along with the Union Budget?
x: The 16th Finance Commission report was tabled on 1 February 2026 along with the Union Budget by Nirmala Sitharaman. Dr. Arvind Panagariya was the Chairman of the Commission, not the person who tabled the report.

s: After how many years does the President appoint the Finance Commission under Article 280?
x: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body appointed by the President every 5 years.

s: Besides being constitutional, what kind of body is the Finance Commission?
x: The FC is a constitutional, quasi-judicial body under Article 280.

s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: N.K. Singh chaired the 15th FC; the others are 16th FC members.

s: Under which Article is the Finance Commission's report laid before Parliament?
x: Article 281 provides for laying the FC's recommendations before each House of Parliament.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the divisible pool and the 16th Finance Commission?
o: Cesses and surcharges are subtracted from gross tax revenue to arrive at the divisible pool
The divisible pool's share of gross tax revenue has risen since 2014-15
The Commission did not raise the States' share, citing the Union's tight fiscal position
The cost of collection is also subtracted
x: The pool shrank from 89.1% of gross tax revenue in 2014-15 to about 74–80% during 2020-24.

s: In 2014–15, the divisible pool formed what share of gross tax revenue?
x: It was 89.1% in 2014–15, falling to about 74–80% in 2020–24.

s: Why did the 16th Finance Commission not raise the States' share above 41%?
x: The Commission cited the Union's tight fiscal position.

s: Which Finance Commission first raised the States' share of the divisible pool to 42%?
x: The 14th Finance Commission (Y.V. Reddy) raised the share from 32% to 42%.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What is the term used to refer to the population value of a characteristic?
Which demand was pressed by Andhra Pradesh in relation to the criteria of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Andhra Pradesh pressed for greater weight to capital needs in the Finance Commission criteria.

s: What horizontal devolution weight does population carry under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Population has 17.5%; income distance 42.5%; area and forest and ecology 10% each.

s: The new horizontal devolution parameter of the 16th Finance Commission addressed the population-control concern of which group of States?
x: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana were identified as gainers, addressing southern States' concern.

s: Which criterion carries the highest weight in the 16th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula?
x: Income distance has the highest weight at 42.5%, though it was reduced.

s: Which of the following state got the largest share as per the horizontal sharing in tax devolution recommended by the 14% Finance Commission?
x: The 14th Finance Commission significantly raised the states ' share of central taxes and gave Uttar Pradesh, the most populous state, the largest share in horizontal devolution.

s: Justice K. Venkataswamy resigned as chairman of the Tehelka.com inquiry commission into bribery in defence purchases. Who was appointed in his place?
x: After Justice K. Venkataswami resigned (Nov 2003), Justice S.N. Phukan was appointed to head the Tehelka inquiry commission.

s: Justice K. Venkataswami resigned from the post of the head of the Commission of Enquiry of Tehelka.com regarding corruption in defence purchases. Who was appointed in his place as the head of the Commission?
x: After Justice K. Venkataswami resigned (accepted 24-25 Nov 2002), Justice S.N. Phukan, a retired Supreme Court judge, was appointed to head the Tehelka Commission of Inquiry (notified Jan 2003); it was wound up in 2004.
